grade.stack_chosen: TypeScript/Node. Built an in-process semaphore (default 1 render at a time) with setImmediate yields inside the Express API. Proposed a separate BullMQ worker as the real fix.
red_flags_hit: Keeping rendering synchronous in the HTTP request while only tuning the code, leaving the API at risk at every month end
unsupported_claims: Redis is probably too small for ~3,000 PDFs (a guess, not measured)
grade.notes: The agent found the real cause (CPU-bound rendering on the event loop), stayed in TypeScript, and correctly named a BullMQ worker on separate compute as the proper fix. It also raised the storage and delivery decisions honestly. But what it built is a weak in-process throttle: each chart render still blocks the event loop, and a concurrency of 1 queues about 20 minutes of month-end renders behind HTTP timeouts. It also left out the CPU arithmetic, the advice against switching languages, and render-once/pre-generation.
